title: Related-Key Security of Full-State Keyed Sponge and Duplex
summary: A known XOR-related-key query pair gives a trivial collision for FKS; a thorough related-key security analysis of full-state keyed Sponge and Duplex remains open.

formal_statement.body: Can full-state keyed Sponge and Duplex constructions, including the full-state keyed Sponge construction $\text{FKS}$, be given a thorough related-key security analysis when an adversary has access to instances keyed with related keys and knows the XOR relation $\Delta = K_1 \oplus K_2$ between two keys? The unresolved task is to characterize security in that model and account for the concrete trivial collision attack in which the adversary queries $\text{FKS}$ under $K_1$ on $M$ and $\text{FKS}$ under $K_2$ on $M \oplus \Delta$, producing colliding outputs; only informal countermeasures against such trivial attacks are proposed, rather than a thorough related-key treatment.

scope.domain: Related-key security of full-state keyed Sponge and Duplex constructions, including FKS, in symmetric cryptography.
assumptions: The adversary can access instances keyed by related keys and knows their XOR relation.
parameters: K₁ and K₂ are the two related keys, and Δ denotes their known XOR relation
M is the first query input, while M ⊕ Δ is the paired input used in the collision attack
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop a thorough security characterization in the related-key model that accounts for the trivial XOR-based collision attack.

citations.label: Security of Full-State Keyed Sponge and Duplex: Applications to Authenticated Encryption

progress.summary: The source gives a concrete trivial collision attack under related keys and proposes only informal countermeasures. It leaves a thorough related-key security treatment outside its scope.
